# Why the Sky is Blue

## For a 3-Year-Old Toddler
The sun sends us lots of colors. When the light hits the air, the blue color gets bounced around everywhere like a little bouncy ball. So, when you look up, you see all that bounced blue color!

## For a High School Teenager
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. As sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere, it hits gas molecules and spreads in all directions. Blue light travels in shorter, smaller waves than other colors, so it is scattered much more than red or yellow, which is why our eyes see a blue hue across the sky during the day.

## For a Physics PhD
The blue color of the sky is primarily due to Rayleigh scattering, where electromagnetic radiation interacts with particles much smaller than the wavelength of the light. Since the scattering intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength ($I \propto \lambda^{-4}$), the shorter-wavelength end of the spectrum (blue and violet) is scattered significantly more efficiently than longer wavelengths. While violet is scattered even more, the human eye's sensitivity to blue and the solar spectral distribution result in the observed azure color.
